agree.reason: The match and the per-child numbers are concrete, but a reader who left over Eastside gets one sentence of acknowledgment and is then told to 'think about these kids', which may feel like being guilted rather than won back.

honest.reason: The draft drops the brief's false 'guarantees every child' claim and gives the true 26-child figure, though the P.S. says 'any gift' is doubled without repeating the $15,000 cap.

works_the_facts.reason: The $170 ≈ two months, $575 → one year and $30,000 → 26 children figures are all correctly derived, but the draft never sets the full $30,000 against what this group has actually given (9 gifts and $1,240 last year, $28,900 even if all 340 gave $85), so the 26-child outcome looks more likely than it is.

right_comparison.reason: It never says what happens if the match isn't met, or that even a full match leaves 35 of the 61 children still waiting, so the reader can't see the real alternative.

qualification.reason: The conditional 'if we meet the full match' comes with a date (December 31), a number ($15,000/$30,000) and a consequence (26 children), but it doesn't say what a partial result would mean.

objections.reason: The Eastside grievance is named and then set aside with no explanation of why the branch closed and no sign that anything has changed, and the 'some of you' wording in a personal email reads as a mass message to the very reader most likely to forward it with comments.

fit.reason: It is a year-end email of roughly 200 words with a subject line, a call-to-action button and a P.S., signed by the executive director as the brief asked.
